math-bit-manipulation__single-number-ii-.title: Single Number II / III
math-bit-manipulation__single-number-ii-.statement: **II:** every element appears **three times** except one (which appears once) — find that single element. **III:** every element appears twice except **two** singletons — find both of them, in any order.

examples.explanation: 3 and 5 each appear once; the rest appear twice.

constraints: II: 1 <= nums.length <= 3*10^4, each value appears three times except one that appears once
III: exactly two elements appear once, all others appear exactly twice

approaches.name: II — two-state ones/twos machine
approaches.idea: For each bit position, the number of set bits across all numbers is a multiple of 3 plus the single number's bit. The `ones/twos` bitmask pair tracks which bits have been seen once vs twice and clears them once a bit is seen a third time, so after the loop `ones` holds exactly the unique number.

approaches.name: III — XOR all, split by a differing bit
approaches.idea: XOR of everything equals `a ^ b`, the XOR of the two singletons (all paired values cancel). Any set bit in it differs between `a` and `b`; take the lowest set bit via `x & (-x)` and partition all numbers into two groups by that bit. XOR within each group isolates one singleton.

math-bit-manipulation__single-number-ii-.insight: II: "appears 3x" ⇒ per-bit counts mod 3 via the ones/twos state machine that clears at 3. III: XOR gives a^b, and any set bit there separates the two singletons into independent XOR groups; x & (-x) isolates the lowest set bit.

math-bit-manipulation__maximum-xor-of-tw.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
math-bit-manipulation__maximum-xor-of-tw.pattern: Greedy bit-by-bit with prefix set (or bitwise trie)
math-bit-manipulation__maximum-xor-of-tw.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum result of `nums[i] XOR nums[j]` over all pairs `i, j`.

examples.explanation: Only one element; XOR with itself is 0.

approaches.name: Greedy from the highest bit using a prefix set
approaches.idea: Build the answer one bit at a time from the most significant bit down. At each step assume the next bit of the answer can be 1: collect all number prefixes under the current mask into a set, and check whether two prefixes exist whose XOR equals the candidate (using `a ^ b == c` iff `a ^ c == b`). If such a pair exists, keep that bit set.

math-bit-manipulation__maximum-xor-of-tw.insight: Maximize XOR greedily from the top bit: for each bit, test whether some pair of masked prefixes can realize a 1 there, using a^b=c ⟺ a^c=b to probe a HashSet in O(1).

math-bit-manipulation__sum-of-two-intege.title: Sum of Two Integers
math-bit-manipulation__sum-of-two-intege.statement: Compute the sum of two integers `a` and `b` **without using the operators `+` and `-`**.

approaches.name: XOR for sum-without-carry, AND<<1 for carry
approaches.idea: `a ^ b` adds the bits ignoring carry, while `(a & b) << 1` is the carry that must still be added. Repeat, feeding the carry back in, until the carry becomes zero. Java's two's-complement `int` handles negative values and overflow wraparound automatically.

math-bit-manipulation__sum-of-two-intege.insight: Addition = XOR (sum without carry) plus (AND << 1) (the carry), looped until no carry remains.

math-bit-manipulation__counting-bits.title: Counting Bits
math-bit-manipulation__counting-bits.statement: Given an integer `n`, return an array `ans` of length `n + 1` where `ans[i]` is the number of set bits (1s) in the binary representation of `i`.

approaches.name: DP using i >> 1
approaches.idea: The number of set bits in `i` equals the set bits in `i >> 1` (dropping the lowest bit) plus the lowest bit itself (`i & 1`). Since `i >> 1 < i`, the value is already computed, giving a single O(n) pass.

math-bit-manipulation__counting-bits.insight: popcount(i) = popcount(i >> 1) + (i & 1): reuse the answer for the number with its lowest bit removed.

math-bit-manipulation__subsets-via-bitma.title: Subsets via bitmask
math-bit-manipulation__subsets-via-bitma.statement: Given an array `nums` of distinct integers, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution must not contain duplicate subsets.
constraints: All elements of nums are unique

approaches.name: Iterate every bitmask from 0 to 2^n - 1
approaches.idea: Each subset corresponds to an n-bit mask: bit `i` set means `nums[i]` is included. Loop over all `2^n` masks and, for each, collect the elements whose bit is set. This enumerates the power set directly with no recursion.

math-bit-manipulation__subsets-via-bitma.insight: A subset of an n-element set is exactly an n-bit mask; loop 0..2^n-1 and include nums[i] whenever bit i is set.

math-bit-manipulation__bitwise-and-of-ra.title: Bitwise AND of Range
math-bit-manipulation__bitwise-and-of-ra.pattern: Common binary prefix of the range endpoints
math-bit-manipulation__bitwise-and-of-ra.statement: Given two integers `left` and `right` (with `left <= right`), return the bitwise AND of all numbers in the inclusive range `[left, right]`.

approaches.name: Shift until endpoints share a common prefix
approaches.idea: AND over a range is 1 in a bit only if that bit is 1 in every number, which happens exactly on the common high-order prefix of `left` and `right`; all lower bits vary within the range and get zeroed. Right-shift both until they are equal (that shared prefix), counting the shifts, then shift back.

math-bit-manipulation__bitwise-and-of-ra.insight: The AND of a range is the common binary prefix of its endpoints, with all lower (varying) bits cleared.

math-bit-manipulation__minimum-xor-sum-b.title: Minimum XOR Sum / Beautiful Arrangement
math-bit-manipulation__minimum-xor-sum-b.statement: **Minimum XOR Sum:** given equal-length arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, rearrange `nums2` to minimize `sum(nums1[i] XOR nums2[i])`; return that minimum. **Beautiful Arrangement:** count permutations `perm` of `1..n` such that for every 1-indexed position `i`, either `perm[i] % i == 0` or `i % perm[i] == 0`.
constraints: Min XOR Sum: 1 <= n <= 14, 0 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 10^7

approaches.name: Min XOR Sum — bitmask DP over used nums2 indices
approaches.idea: `dp[mask]` = minimum XOR sum after assigning the first `popcount(mask)` entries of `nums1`, where `mask` marks which `nums2` indices are used. The next `nums1` index is `Integer.bitCount(mask)`; try pairing it with each still-free `nums2[j]`, transitioning to `mask | (1<<j)`. Answer is `dp[(1<<n)-1]`.

approaches.name: Beautiful Arrangement — bitmask DP counting permutations
approaches.idea: `dp[mask]` = number of ways to fill the first `popcount(mask)` positions using exactly the numbers in `mask`. The next position is `pos = popcount(mask) + 1`; for each unused number `num` that is divisibility-compatible with `pos`, add `dp[mask]` into `dp[mask | (1<<(num-1))]`. Answer is `dp[(1<<n)-1]`.

math-bit-manipulation__minimum-xor-sum-b.insight: Both are assignment problems over 1..n: let dp[mask] describe having placed popcount(mask) items; the next slot index is popcount(mask), and you extend by any unused element — O(n·2^n) beats O(n!) permutation search.

math-bit-manipulation__power-of-two-powe.title: Power of Two / Power of Three / Power of Four
math-bit-manipulation__power-of-two-powe.pattern: Bit tricks and divisibility by the largest power
math-bit-manipulation__power-of-two-powe.statement: Determine whether a given integer `n` is a power of two, a power of three, or a power of four respectively (i.e. `n == b^x` for some integer `x >= 0`).

approaches.name: Bit trick (2 & 4) and largest-power divisibility (3)
approaches.idea: A power of two has exactly one set bit: `n > 0 && (n & (n-1)) == 0`. A power of four is additionally a power of two whose single set bit lies on an even position, tested with mask `0x55555555`. For power of three there is no bit pattern, so use that `1162261467 = 3^19` is the largest power of three fitting in an `int`; `n` is a power of three iff it is positive and divides it evenly.

math-bit-manipulation__power-of-two-powe.insight: Power of two ⇒ (n & (n-1))==0; power of four ⇒ that plus the bit in mask 0x55555555; power of three ⇒ divides 3^19 (1162261467), the max power of 3 in an int.

math-bit-manipulation__pow-x-n.title: Pow(x,n)
math-bit-manipulation__pow-x-n.statement: Implement `pow(x, n)`, which computes `x` raised to the power `n` (i.e. `x^n`).

approaches.name: Binary exponentiation
approaches.idea: Square the base while halving the exponent: whenever the current low bit of the exponent is 1, multiply it into the result. Promote `n` to a `long` before negating so that `Integer.MIN_VALUE` does not overflow when handling negative exponents (a negative `n` means the reciprocal `1/x`).

math-bit-manipulation__pow-x-n.insight: Binary exponentiation: multiply in x^(2^k) whenever bit k of n is set, O(log n); widen n to long before negating to survive Integer.MIN_VALUE.
